# Uncloud Cluster Management

Curated by Skill Harbor: a reference for managing Uncloud clusters, a decentralised self-hosting platform running Docker containers over a WireGuard mesh with Caddy as reverse proxy. No central control plane: every machine is an equal cluster member, services communicate on the overlay network (10.210.0.0/16 by default, DNS inside the mesh), and Caddy runs globally to terminate public HTTP/HTTPS traffic with auto-obtained Let's Encrypt TLS. Deploy services from Compose files with `uc deploy`, run one-off services with `uc service run`, publish HTTP, HTTPS, TCP or UDP ports through Uncloud, configure Caddy ingress with `x-caddy`, `x-ports` or `--caddyfile` (the Caddyfile is autogenerated, never edit it directly), add static proxy routes for non-cluster LAN devices, bootstrap or join machines with `uc machine init` / `uc machine add`, and inspect logs, service state, volumes, DNS and machine placement. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: you need the `uc` CLI installed and machines that can run Docker; this is real self-hosting with real machines on a real network, so broken networking means unreachable services, test changes on one machine first. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
